title.narrative: Effective and inclusive labour market institutions that support an improved design, implementation and monitoring of wage policies

description.narrative:
Egypt has made significant progress in establishing and adjusting the minimum wage in recent years. Introduced in the private sector in January 2022 at EGP 2,400 per month, it has since been revised upward several times, reaching EGP 7,000 as of March 2025 to reinforce wage protection. However, emerging challenges related to methodology, implementation, compliance, and institutional coordination have highlighted the need to strengthen the minimum wage system. These challenges include ambiguity in wage components, the treatment of bonuses and in-kind benefits, variations in compliance across enterprises, and limited clarity on how minimum wages should be adjusted over time.
At the same time, broader socioeconomic factors such as inflationary pressures, disparities across sectors and regions, varying enterprise capacities, and labor market informality pose constraints to the effective and sustainable adoption of minimum wage policies. These dynamics require a more structured, evidence-based approach to wage determination that balances the needs of workers and their families with economic conditions and enterprise sustainability.
In response, the ILO supports national stakeholders in strengthening the minimum wage system through a comprehensive and evidence-based approach. This includes defining a transparent methodology for determining and adjusting minimum wages, identifying appropriate arrangements and gradual steps for implementation, assessing the feasibility of sectoral and geographical adaptations, and analyzing the expected benefits, risks, and mitigation strategies associated with reforms.
The intervention combines technical analysis, international comparative experience, stakeholder consultations, and capacity-building activities to support informed decision-making and effective social dialogue. It will also contribute to improving the evidence base for wage policy, including through the use of labor market data and analytical tools.
